1 · The story: what UX-4 is and what you are asked

Meridian Home Comfort is a made-up heating and cooling company. This project builds an assistant that talks to its customers, books visits, and hands the customer to a person when it should.

Where we were

Over the last two days we wrote down what the screens should say and do (UX-1 to UX-3). UX-3 gave 12 screen specs, a look called A5 Service desk, and a signed list of calls between the screens and the back end (CON-1 to CON-22 and an OpenAPI file). You signed UX-3 on 2026-10-21.

What UX-4 is

UX-4 is a clickable version of those 12 screens, built in the real front-end folder (apps/web/) but talking to a mock, not a real server. A mock is a stand-in that answers from the signed contract file. Fake staff, a fake clock and scripted situations (a safety message, a failed join, an overdue case) are added by a dev layer that only exists while you test and is left out of the real build. Five build groups made the screens; an integrator pass joined them.

Why a person has to look

Tests can show that a button exists and a sentence matches the spec. They cannot show whether a sentence is clear to a stranger, whether the safety message stands out, or whether the queue feels calm or cluttered. For that, someone has to click through it, in the same order a customer, a representative, a supervisor and an owner would.

What you are asked

Is it understandable and visually appropriate? Work through section 3 and say what feels wrong. Then answer the nine decisions in section 6, some of which are wording only you can judge. This page does not sign UX-4, and the checklist is not ticked.

2 · How to run it

Two terminals on the server, one tunnel from your laptop. Fact PROTOTYPE_PLAN.md and apps/web/README.md.

cd apps/web
npm run mock        # Prism on http://127.0.0.1:4019 (terminal 1)
npm run dev:mock    # Vite on http://127.0.0.1:5184 (terminal 2)

# from your laptop, in a third terminal:
ssh -L 5184:127.0.0.1:5184 claude-vultr

Then open http://127.0.0.1:5184. On the server itself, the same address works.

Logging in Fact

The first page is the demo login (SCR-12). In mock mode any non-empty username and password is accepted. The real shared demo username and password are not written in apps/web/README.md yet: the spec says the README holds placeholders (<DEMO_USERNAME>, <DEMO_PASSWORD>) until the real ones are set on Railway. Nothing is invented here.

SCREEN_SPECS SCR-12; PROTOTYPE_PLAN.md, What is faked.

Address bar shortcuts Fact

?signedin=1 skips the login. ?scenario=<id> opens one prepared situation. ?role=customer|representative|supervisor|owner sets the role. ?staffing=on|off turns simulated staff on or off. ?theme=light|dark picks a theme. Combine them: /?signedin=1&scenario=scr05.live-queued&theme=dark.

apps/web/README.md, Mock-mode URL parameters. The URL rewrites itself to reproduce the state.

The dev panel (the bar at the bottom that says "Prototype only")

It collapses to a small pill. Open it and you get five tabs. It is only in the mock build.

States

Jump to a screen, then pick one of its scenarios, grouped by the eight standard states (default, empty, loading, partial, error, stale, success, disabled). Greyed cells are states that do not apply, with the reason. Also "Anywhere" scenarios such as a session ending or going offline.

Session

Fake sign-in, role, expire the session, refuse the next login, reset the role, restart, theme and a delay slider.

Calls

Every request the screen made: operation, status, which example answered, time. A row marked Drift means a reply broke the contract.

Stream

The live chat events, with buttons to drop and reconnect the stream.

Look

The component kit at /__kit: buttons, cards and fields in one place.

3 · Click-through script, by role

Each screen lists what to do and which prepared situations to open. Open a situation with http://127.0.0.1:5184/?signedin=1&scenario=<id>. At each one, ask: do I know what this says, what to do next, and does it look right? Fact: the scenario ids were read from apps/web/src/dev/scenarios/. The screenshots are the default state, light theme, only.

Customer

SCR-1 · Customer chat

The page a homeowner uses. They type a problem (no cooling, a burning smell), the assistant answers from the knowledge base, offers booking windows, and can hand the customer to a person. Route: /.

  1. Open /?signedin=1&scenario=scr01-core.default. Check the greeting, the demo bar at the top (date and whether anyone is online) and the strip that says what is settled so far.
  2. Safety first: open scr01-cards.safety-takeover, then send any message. The reply should put safety ahead of everything and lock the booking path.
  3. Booking: open scr01-cards.slot-card, send a message, and pick a window. Then try scr01-core.success-booked to see the booked card and the settled panel.
  4. Talking to a person: scr01-core.success-live-queued (staff on shift) and scr01-core.success-handoff (nobody online). The wording should be honest about who is, or is not, coming.
  5. Trouble: scr01-core.error-send-failed, scr01-core.flow-limit-rate, scr01-core.flow-session-ended, scr01-core.disabled-chat-closed.

Scenario ids you can paste after ?signedin=1&scenario=: scr01-core.default scr01-core.empty scr01-core.loading-replying scr01-core.success-booked scr01-core.success-change-request scr01-core.flow-safety-takeover scr01-cards.safety-takeover scr01-cards.slot-card scr01-cards.code-sent scr01-cards.no-window-fits scr01-cards.out-of-area

Login And Role Switch

SCR-12 · Demo login

The front door to the whole deployment. One shared demo username and password. It says plainly that this is a demonstration, never a Meridian account. Route: /login.

A one-click control in the header of every screen to act as customer, representative, supervisor or owner. There is no second password. The page at /role explains each role. Route: /role.

5 · Browser sweep result

Browser sweep result Fact

Every scenario was opened in Chrome with the accessibility checker (axe, WCAG 2 A/AA) at 1280 and 390 pixels wide, and in dark on desktop. All of it ran against the Prism mock and the dev layer, not a real backend.

  • Desktop: 494 passed, 0 failed. Phone: 257 passed, 0 failed (237 skipped: dark runs on desktop only).
  • Checked on each scenario: no uncaught errors, no contract-drift line, exactly one h1, no sideways scroll, zero axe violations.
  • The first sweep found 66 failing scenarios (labels that did not contain their visible text), one screen with no heading and a missing favicon. All fixed and re-run clean.
  • 15 timed scenarios (10 s, 60 s, 65 s) have only their opening state asserted.
  • Four browser flows pass: chat reply, staff claim, role switch, login return. So does the rehearsal of chat, booking slot conflict, person request, staff claim and join, representative message, hand back and close. In that rehearsal the live messages are injected by the dev layer, so it proves the screens render them, not that a server delivers them.
  • Not verified: anything against a real backend. See docs/ux/04-prototype/INTEGRATION_HANDOFF.md.
  • One thing for you to look at: on a 390 px phone, after "Claim and join" the case stays on the Brief tab and the reply box is under Evidence. A representative must tap Evidence before replying.

6 · The decisions that need your answer

Nine choices. Each tells the story first, then the options, and ends with one question. Answer each on its own. None is answered yet. D-1 and D-2 are wording; D-3 to D-6 are conflicts or gaps in the spec; D-7 to D-9 go to the contract owners.

D-1 · Wording when a claim worked but joining the chat did not (case view) Awaiting you

Where this comes up

A representative opens a case on SCR-6 and presses Claim. The claim goes through, so the case is theirs. Then the second step, joining the customer's live chat, fails (the chat just closed, or the network blinked).

What is open

The spec has no sentence for this half-success. Without one, the screen would say nothing, or would call the whole thing a failure and tempt the representative to claim again. A reviewer would find that confusing. The build session wrote a proposed sentence so the screen is not blank.

Why it is not obvious

It is two facts at once: you own the case, and you are not in the chat. The wording has to say both without alarm and point to the one thing that fixes it, the Join chat button.

Why you are asked

Copy is yours to judge: it is the staff voice the Meridian demo speaks in. The build session may not invent customer-visible or staff-visible wording on its own (SCREEN_SPECS lists every string).

A. Use the proposed sentence: "You claimed this case, but joining the chat didn't go through. Try Join chat."

Ships as built. Plain, names the button.

B. Rewrite it (you give the words)

One short pass, then the string in errorCopy.ts changes.

C. Drop the sentence and show a generic error

Simplest, but loses the fact that the claim worked.

Recommended: A. It says what happened and what to press.

Decision needed: Should the SCR-6 sentence be A (as proposed), B (your words) or C (generic error)?

D-2 · Wording when a claim worked but joining the chat did not (queue) Awaiting you

Where this comes up

The same half-success, but the claim was made from a row on the queue (SCR-5) instead of from inside the case.

What is open

A second sentence was proposed for the queue, because the representative is not on the case page yet. It says to open the case first: "You claimed the case, but joining the chat didn't go through. Open it and try Join chat."

Why it is not obvious

The two screens differ by one step (open the case), so the sentences differ by a few words. Keeping them separate is a choice; one shared sentence would be shorter but wrong on one of the screens.

Why you are asked

Same reason as D-1, and it is a separate choice. One yes to D-1 does not answer this one.

A. Use the proposed queue sentence as built

Accurate for the queue.

B. Rewrite it (you give the words)

Same small pass as D-1.

C. Use the SCR-6 sentence on both screens

One string to maintain; slightly off on the queue because it does not say to open the case.

Recommended: A.

Decision needed: Should the SCR-5 sentence be A (as proposed), B (your words) or C (reuse the SCR-6 sentence)?

D-3 · After a demo reset, which role does the reviewer have? Awaiting you

Where this comes up

You are acting as Supervisor on SCR-7 and press Reset the demo on SCR-3 to start a clean run. The reset ends all open chats and clears case state.

What is open

SCREEN_SPECS (N-14, SCR-3 R6) says the reset keeps your role. The signed OpenAPI file and CON-9 say the role goes back to Customer, and the login stays. The two documents disagree. The build followed the OpenAPI file, because the mock is generated from it and the backend will be too. After a reset the page re-reads the session and adds a sentence saying the role changed.

Why it is not obvious

Both are defensible. Keeping the role saves one click. Going back to Customer matches a fresh start and what the backend contract says. Changing the contract would reopen UX-3, which is signed.

Why you are asked

This is a conflict between two documents you signed at UX-3, so the build could not settle it quietly in the screen's favour.

A. Keep what is built: role returns to Customer, login stays; fix SCREEN_SPECS to match the contract

No contract change. The reviewer clicks one role button after a reset.

B. Change the contract so the role is kept

Nicer after a reset, but it reopens CON-9 and the backend plan.

Recommended: A. It costs one click and avoids reopening a signed contract.

Decision needed: After Reset the demo, should the role return to Customer (A, as built) or stay as it was (B)?

D-4 · One sentence for every login refusal Awaiting you

Where this comes up

On SCR-12 someone types a wrong username, a wrong password, or tries too many times, or the form is incomplete.

What is open

The spec allows one refusal sentence for the first three: "That username or password didn't work. Check the README and try again." The contract also has a separate rate-limit sentence (UI_CONTRACTS differs from SCREEN_SPECS here). The build used the one sentence for every failure so nothing reveals which part was wrong or that a throttle kicked in.

Why it is not obvious

Telling someone they are rate limited is helpful to a real person but tells an attacker something. In a demo with one shared login the attacker risk is small. It is a copy and security-posture call.

Why you are asked

It trades helpfulness for sameness, and the spec and the contract disagree. That needs a ruling, not a quiet pick.

A. One sentence for every refusal (as built)

Same sentence, same timing; matches SCREEN_SPECS.

B. Keep the one sentence for wrong credentials but show the contract's own rate-limit sentence when throttled

Friendlier; one more string; reveals the throttle.

Recommended: A.

Decision needed: Should every login failure give the same sentence (A) or should a throttle get its own (B)?

D-5 · The demo-date explainer on SCR-3 Awaiting you

Where this comes up

On the demo guide page, IA.md lists a line saying what the demo date is and how the clock moves (it is Fri Oct 16, 2026 at the start and moves when the supervisor presses +1 hour).

What is open

SCREEN_SPECS has no wording for it, so the build did not make it up. The demo bar at the top of every screen already shows the date.

Why it is not obvious

Without the line, a first-time reviewer sees a date that is not today with no reason given, until they read the guide cards. With it, SCR-3 gets one more paragraph that someone must write.

Why you are asked

Wording for a page the reviewer reads is your call, and leaving it out is a departure from the information architecture you signed.

A. Leave it out; the demo bar is enough

No work. Risk: the odd date looks like a bug.

B. Write one sentence and add it to SCR-3 (you or Claude drafts, you approve)

Small change; clears up the date.

Recommended: B, drafted by Claude for your review.

Decision needed: Add a demo-date explainer to SCR-3 (B) or leave it out (A)?

D-6 · Owner navigation: "Outcomes · Review list" Awaiting you

Where this comes up

The business owner needs a way to move between their outcomes page (SCR-9) and the flag review list (SCR-8) in the staff header.

What is open

The information architecture gives no navigation for the owner. The UX-4 plan proposes two links, Outcomes and Review list. It is the plan's own choice, not yours or the spec's.

Why it is not obvious

Fewer links keep the owner's header calm; more links make the review list easy to find. It is cheap to change later, but it is a visible piece of the interface.

Why you are asked

Navigation labels shape how the owner reads the product, and nobody signed them.

A. Keep "Outcomes · Review list" as built

No work.

B. Outcomes only; the review list is reached from the outcomes page

Simpler header; one fewer way in.

C. You give the labels

One short pass.

Recommended: A.

Decision needed: Which owner navigation should we keep: A (Outcomes and Review list), B (Outcomes only) or C (yours)?

D-7 · Contract gaps the prototype ran into Awaiting you

Where this comes up

While building against the signed OpenAPI file, the groups found places where the screen needs something the contract does not provide, so the mock uses a stand-in. They are listed in docs/ux/04-prototype/groups/*.md and PROTOTYPE_PLAN.md. They are: QueueRow.version (so Assign needs no extra read), Flag.message_text (to expand a flagged message inline), EvalMeasure.definition (so measure definitions come from the data), SettledVisit start and end as ISO times (so the visit window can be a proper time element), retry_turn_id on the timeout notice (so Retry knows which turn), the emergency-window label (a note on the slot card saying it is a regular booking, not emergency service), CANCELLED.settled.actions (the cancel write is missing, so the live mock shows only "There's no fee."), and a few missing examples (quick checks, setStaffing off with nobody waiting, the owner read-only case, SUPERVISOR and OWNER sessions).

What is open

Each gap has a stand-in in the dev layer, so the prototype looks right now. The real backend (Stage 7) will not have the stand-ins. If the contract stays as is, those screens will lose detail or need extra calls.

Why it is not obvious

The contract is signed (UX-3). A change to it reopens UX-3 and breaks the generated types UX-4 pinned. Some gaps are small (a field), some change what a screen can show.

Why you are asked

The contract owners are you and the Stage 7 build. The build session may not edit the OpenAPI file, so it only reports the gaps.

A. Send all the gaps to the contract owners as one change request after UX-4 closes, before Stage 7 builds the matching endpoints

One contract revision; screens lose their stand-ins cleanly.

B. Fix only the ones that change behaviour now (retry_turn_id, CANCELLED.settled.actions, QueueRow.version) and defer the rest

Smaller change; some screens stay trimmed.

C. Leave the contract alone and keep the stand-ins as documented limits

No reopening; the real UI is a little poorer than the prototype.

Recommended: B, with the others queued for the same change request if you want them.

Decision needed: How should we handle the contract gaps: A (all), B (only the behaviour ones), or C (none)?

D-8 · Fee-bearing change: due Friday Oct 16 or Saturday Oct 17? Awaiting you

Where this comes up

The fee-bearing change case (scr06.flow-fee-bearing, case MHC-C-0009) shows a due time at the top of the case view. This is the case where a customer asks to change a booked visit in a way that carries a fee, so a person must handle it.

What is open

SCREEN_SPECS prints the due time as "Due Fri Oct 16 · 12:00 pm". The signed OpenAPI example says "Sat Oct 17 · 12:00 pm, the window start" (due_at 2026-10-17T12:00). The prototype shows what the contract example says, because the screen reads it from the data. So the build and the spec disagree by one day.

Why it is not obvious

D-9 · Inter font: single-storey "a" is not applied Awaiting you

Where this comes up

The design asks for the font Inter with its cv11 setting, which should give a single-storey letter a (this is the plan's reading of the feature). The prototype loads Inter from the @fontsource latin files.

What is open

Those files do not contain the cv11 feature, so the setting does nothing and every a is double-storey. Self-hosting the full Inter file would fix it, at the cost of a bigger font download. The plan defers this to UX-5.

Why it is not obvious

It is a small visual difference that few people would notice, but the design asks for it (design.md section 3.1 asks for the fonts at UX-4), and a bigger font file slows the first load on a phone.

Why you are asked

Whether the single-storey a is worth the extra weight is a look-and-feel judgement.

A. Defer to UX-5 as planned

No change now; you see the double-storey a in the prototype.

B. Self-host the full Inter file now

Matches design.md; bigger download.

C. Drop the cv11 requirement from design.md

No download cost; the design text changes.

Recommended: A.

Decision needed: Should the Inter cv11 gap be deferred (A), fixed now (B) or dropped from the design (C)?
